grammar.title: Determiners
grammar.short: all, both, each, every, either, neither, none, no, whole

slides.sub: Game on: every player, both teams, neither option
slides.hook: Do all your friends play video games? Are both of your parents competitive?

rows: Both games are entertaining. / Both of them are entertaining.
not one and not the other
Neither competitor won. / Neither of us won.
All the competitors start with three lives.
all, seen as a group (+ singular)
Every level is a new challenge.
Each player has a different identity.
There are no saves left. / None of my friends find it addictive.

p: 'the whole' + singular countable noun = all of something.
ex: I played **the whole** game in one weekend – I lost track of time!
I've played **all** the games in the series.
We spent **all day** gaming. = **the whole day**

p: Before pronouns (us, you, them) we must use 'of'.
Before 'the', 'my', 'these', 'of' is usual (but optional with all / both).
ex: **Both of us** were over the moon after our victory.
**Neither of them** knew the truth about the plot.
**Each of the** levels is harder than the last.

slides.title: Shadow Quest: 9/10
text: **Every** level is a challenge, and **each** character has a special strength. You can play with **either** the knight or the thief – **both** are fun!
**All** my friends love the plot, which is full of mystery. **None of** us expected the ending!
The only problem? The game crashed twice, and **neither** time could I save. In a nutshell: it's addictive, entertaining and great for hand-eye coordination.

items: Both of they are good competitors.
Both of them are good competitors.
I liked neither game. / I didn't like either game.

slides.e: Not one and not the other → neither.

slides.q: ___ competitor in the tournament gets a medal.

p: Three or more: all, every, each, none.
of + pronoun: both of us, none of them.

grammar.title: Relative clauses
grammar.short: Defining and non-defining: who, which, that, where, whose, when

slides.sub: Game on: the hero who saved the kingdom
slides.hook: Describe your favourite game character without saying their name. Can your partner guess who it is?

rows: The competitor who takes the most risks usually wins.
The game which I bought is really addictive.
It's the level that always crashes.
This is the castle where the mystery begins.
She's the hero whose identity is a secret.
I remember the day when I won my first victory.

p: They give essential information: which person or thing we mean. No commas.
We can omit who / which / that when it is the object of the clause.
ex: The game **that** I played yesterday was really educational.
The game **(that)** I played yesterday was really educational.
The person **who** developed Minecraft is Swedish.

p: They give extra information. We put them between commas. We can't use 'that' and we can't omit the pronoun.
ex: Tetris, **which** was created in 1984, is still entertaining.
My cousin Lucía, **who** is a pro gamer, has amazing hand-eye coordination.
Japan, **where** many famous games were developed, is my dream trip.

rows: My brother who lives in Paris plays chess. (I have more than one brother)
My brother, who lives in Paris, plays chess. (I have only one brother)

slides.title: The Lost Kingdom
text: Mira is a girl **who** lives in a world **where** the sun never rises. Her father, **whose** sword is magic, disappeared on the night **when** the darkness began.
Mira finds a map **which** shows the way to the Tower of Truth. The journey, **which** is full of danger, will test her strength.
The player **who** helps Mira must make choices **that** change the plot. Will she find justice – or loss?

items: Zelda, that is my favourite game, is quite old.
Zelda, which is my favourite game, is quite old.
The man which designed the plot is famous.
The man who designed the plot is famous.
This is the level where I always lose there.
This is the level where I always lose.

slides.q: That's the gamer ___ videos have 10 million views.
Fortnite, ___ came out in 2017, is free to play.
slides.e: Non-defining clause with commas → which (not that).

p: who = people, which = things, where = places, whose = possession, when = time.
Defining: essential info, no commas, 'that' is OK.

This is the console ___ I got for my birthday.

He's the boy ___ sister won the tournament.

A controller is a thing ___ you use to play.
